papers.title: Effects of Mindfulness Training on Impulsivity and NoGo-Go-Related Brain Activation in Internet Gaming Disorder.
papers.reason: The paper studies inhibitory control and impulsivity using a Go/NoGo brain activation paradigm in a clinical human group, directly relevant to executive control mechanisms.

papers.title: Combined Neuromelanin-Sensitive and Functional Magnetic Resonance Imaging Links Midbrain Dopaminergic Dysfunction to Connectome Architecture in First-Episode, Medication-Naïve Major Depressive Disorder.
papers.reason: The paper is human clinical neuroimaging in depression but does not appear to focus on planning, working memory, attention, cognitive control, or cognitive assessment.

papers.title: Esketamine attenuates postoperative cognitive dysfunction in association with restoration of locus coeruleus–mPFC noradrenergic signaling in aged mice
papers.reason: Animal evidence linking noradrenergic locus coeruleus-mPFC signaling to postoperative cognitive dysfunction is relevant to cognitive impairment mechanisms but only indirectly tied to executive-function modelling.

papers.title: Cognitive and neural outcomes of executive function training in healthy adults: a systematic review
papers.reason: A systematic review of cognitive and neural effects of executive-function training is directly relevant to behavioural and neural mechanisms of executive control.

papers.title: Network-related variations of cerebrovascular status are correlated with cognitive control performance
papers.reason: The paper links regional cerebrovascular network status to proactive and reactive cognitive control in a task-switching paradigm, providing empirical constraints for models of executive control.

papers.title: P029 | MIDBRAIN DOPAMINE DEPLETION ALTERS MEDIAL PREFRONTAL CORTEX FUNCTION: INVESTIGATED BY IN VIVO THREE-PHOTON IMAGING AND EX VIVO PATCH-CLAMP RECORDINGS
papers.reason: The study provides animal neural evidence that dopamine loss disrupts mPFC circuit dynamics relevant to working memory and executive control, though it lacks direct executive-task modelling or behavioural assessment.

papers.title: Attentional prioritization enhances the accessibility of neural representations during working memory maintenance
papers.reason: This is a central EEG and behavioural study of how attention modulates working-memory maintenance and representational accessibility, directly informing models of attention and working memory.

papers.title: An electrophysiological investigation of inhibitory control in children with dyslexia and the role of comorbid ADHD symptoms: a pilot randomized intervention study.
papers.reason: The paper uses ERP measures during a Go/No-Go task to study inhibitory control in children with dyslexia and ADHD symptoms, making it strongly relevant to neural assessment of executive function.

papers.title: EEG Decoding in Context: A Framework for Tuning-Free EEG Foundation Models
papers.reason: The paper develops a general EEG decoding framework potentially useful for cognitive assessment, but its core contribution is a foundation-model method rather than executive-function modelling or clinical biomarker validation.

papers.title: Alzheimer detection using multivariate decomposition of EEG signals and a novel BPGA feature selection with HGBoost classifier: overall, LNSO and lobe-wise analysis
papers.reason: An EEG-based machine-learning approach for Alzheimer detection is relevant to digital biomarkers for cognitive impairment, though it is not specifically focused on executive-function modelling.
